title: Ephemeral domain-claiming and invite delegation guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a coherent set of admin guardrails for org/team onboarding: (1) a DNS/email domain attestation flow that supports ephemeral (temporary) invitation tokens which auto-expire, (2) delegation model to allow scoped invite rights to team leads without granting full org admin, and (3) enforceable email allowlist/denylist rules tied to attestation state. This work ties RBAC v2 assertions to invite capability and expands audit logging to capture attestation and delegation events for compliance and incident postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /orgs/:org/attestations creates a domain attestation and returns verification tokens (DNS and email) and audit-id
UI: Org settings shows domain as Unverified / Pending / Verified and displays verification method and expiry for ephemeral tokens
Invites created with ephemeral tokens expire after configurable TTL (default 72 hours) and are rejected server-side post-expiry
Delegation: Org admins can grant a 'team_invite' RBAC v2 permission scoped to a team; scoped invitees cannot escalate to org-admin or view audit logs
Allowlist enforcement: When 'require_domain_attestation' is on, invites from emails outside verified domains are blocked unless a manual exception is logged by an admin

Audit logging: Every attestation action (create, token issued, token validated, token expired), invite creation (including delegated actor), invite acceptance, and manual exception is emitted with structured fields: actor, org_id, domain, method, token_id, ttl, result
Backward compatibility: Existing invite endpoints continue to work; legacy tokens are mapped to expiry metadata and invalidated if older than 180 days
E2E test coverage for API, UI flow, and audit event emission exists and is green in CI
tasks: Design: finalize UI mockups and copy for domain attestation states (DES-1192) - link in notes
Backend: schema changes for attestation table (domain, method, token_id, issued_at, expires_at, status, audit_id)
Backend: invite token lifecycle logic (issue, validate, auto-expire), tie to RBAC v2 permission checks
Backend: audit-event producer for attestation and delegated-invite events
Sync: update allowlist/denylist service to be evaluated during invite flow
Auth: map new 'team_invite' permission into RBAC v2 policy engine and update enforcer
Frontend: settings page components and invite modal changes to surface token TTL and verification status
QA: add tests covering delegation misuse cases (try invite as delegated user for other teams, attempt to escalate)
Ops: migration script to backfill expire timestamps for legacy tokens and a housekeeping worker to sweep expired tokens every 1h
Docs: update Admin docs and API reference for attestation endpoints and delegation semantics
decisions: Use DNS TXT and email verification as parallel methods; prefer DNS for org-owned domains (recommended) and email for smaller teams
Default ephemeral invite TTL set to 72 hours, configurable by org admins up to 14 days
Delegated invite permission is explicit 'team_invite' and cannot co-exist with 'team_admin' without additional approval
Audit events will be written to the existing event stream (kinesis) and persisted to the long-term audit log store with a new schema version
Security review required before rollout to production; feature gated behind runtime flag 'ephemeral_invites_v2'
notes: Related incident: INV-2024-09 noted missing audit entries for manual exceptions — this ticket logs explicit exception events
Compatibility note: Marketplace integrations relying on older invite tokens will be contacted as part of migration plan
Legal asked for retention window of attestation tokens; recommended retention set to 1 year for auditability
